# Public research intake — 2026-10-08

## Scope and registry relationship

This bounded intake resolves the supplied public research leads into the canonical [ExternalWork registry](works.jsonl). It adds 47 Work rows (`KWRK-000084`–`KWRK-000130`): 34 arXiv papers, three other publication records, four pinned software snapshots, and six official model or product pages. Full identities, canonical URLs, authors, dates, source versions, and source notes remain in `works.jsonl`; the [machine-readable intake audit](research-intake-audit-2026-10-08.json) maps only source identity keys to canonical Work IDs and records verification scope and gaps.

The prior public bibliography crosswalk remains a snapshot of its reviewed 186-identity payload. Its generated summary now reflects the current 130-row Works registry, and its existing `arxiv:2410.03529` lead resolves to `KWRK-000096` (*No Need to Talk: Asynchronous Mixture of Language Models*, also known by the method name SMALLTALK LM). The crosswalk is a map; Works remains authoritative.

The intake records source identity and source-attributed context only. It adds no article, `ExternalClaim`, or `KnowledgeEvidence`; it accepts no new project claim and asserts no adoption relationship. It contains no private issue provenance, private identifiers, or inferred private crosswalk. See [public research identity maintenance](../../BUILDING.md#public-research-identity-maintenance) for the ongoing update contract.

## Findings kept within their tested scope

### Low-memory MoE and edge serving

- **Physical capacity is distinct from a memory policy.** D²MoE reports real-device evaluation that includes an RTX 3060 laptop with 6 GB physical VRAM, 32 GB host RAM, and SSD storage; its other platform is a Jetson AGX Orin with 64 GB shared SoC memory. It dynamically changes expert bit width, so quality depends on the selected quantization point; its results are not uniformly lossless. [arXiv record](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.15299v1), `KWRK-000084`.
- **Whole-device RAM is not discrete VRAM.** EdgeMoE evaluates Raspberry Pi 4B and Jetson TX2 systems with 8 GB of system memory and pages experts through storage. It is edge-device work, not an 8 GB discrete-GPU or mixed-cluster result. [arXiv record](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.14352v2), `KWRK-000085`.
- **Cache-aware routing can change choices.** MCCE/Cache-Prior promotes experts already resident in cache. The paper reports physical 12 GB and 16 GB Android devices; on the 12 GB device it reserves 2 GB, leaving a 10 GB application budget. The method changes router ranking and can change outputs; the paper reports minimal quality impact in its tests, not byte-identical output. [arXiv HTML](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.00099), `KWRK-000086`.
- **PowerInfer-2 uses neuron clusters.** It tests 24 GB and 16 GB unified-memory phones with app-available ceilings of 19 GB and 11 GB, and evaluates a 7–19 GB application memory range. Its sparse-neuron scheduling and flash paging are not exact MoE router selection. [arXiv HTML](https://arxiv.org/html/2406.06282), `KWRK-000087`.
- **WiSP’s 8 GB figure is a policy on a 24 GB card.** WiSP reports byte-identical outputs and tests a physical 24 GiB RTX 3090; its 8 GiB budget is an imposed allocation on that same card. The paper does not establish SSD paging or multi-host execution. [arXiv record](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.21868v2), `KWRK-000088`.
- **Other serving results remain configuration-specific.** SSD-LLaMA reports a 5090 plus at most 32 GB host RAM, not an 8 GB card (`KWRK-000089`). OD-MoE’s under-1 GB figure is per edge worker in a ten-node testbed, not total system memory (`KWRK-000090`). Prism’s supplied setup note describes logical servers simulated on one host with four 40 GB A100s; it is not a physical multi-host result (`KWRK-000091`). FineMoE’s abstract confirms a six-GPU testbed; a 6 GB cache budget must not be read as a 6 GB GPU (`KWRK-000092`).
- **FluxMoE version correction.** Its v3 abstract reports GLM-4.5 on eight H20s and Mixtral on two L40S GPUs. The supplied “four 48 GB L40” detail conflicts with that version and is not repeated as a verified setup. [arXiv record](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.02715v3), `KWRK-000094`.
- **Lossy compression and UMA are separate cases.** FloE’s proceedings abstract reports one RTX 3090, deployment with an 11 GB VRAM footprint, and 4.4–7.6% average performance degradation; it is lossy intra-expert compression, not a 12 GB physical card. The supplied exact 12 GB cap remains a full-text check. [PMLR paper](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/zhou25j.html), `KWRK-000112`. ZipMoE is an UMA-targeted system and its repository says discrete-GPU efficiency is not guaranteed. The exact supplied 32/64 GB platform and 10/20 GB imposed-budget matrix remains unresolved pending full-text confirmation. [PMLR paper](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v306/yang26ds.html), `KWRK-000123`; pinned artifact `KWRK-000124`.
- **SwapMoE’s identity is resolved; two setup details are not.** ACL Anthology identifies the paper (`KWRK-000118`), but the supplied Jetson Nano 4 GB and routing-mask output-change details were not independently confirmed from an accessible primary text view. They remain follow-up checks, not claims in this intake.

### Routing among models and modular experts

The resolved source set includes whole-prompt routing or model-composition works: Composition of Experts (`KWRK-000095`), No Need to Talk / SMALLTALK LM (`KWRK-000096`), MoDEM (`KWRK-000097`), Model-GLUE (`KWRK-000098`), Expert Router (`KWRK-000099`), and Zooter (`KWRK-000107`). Their reported tasks and model pools differ; the intake makes no general claim that routing improves every workload.

ME-Switch (`KWRK-000108`) routes among model variants that share base weights and use compressed fine-tune deltas, so it is distinct from composing independent full-model endpoints. FlexOlmo (`KWRK-000100`) independently trains FFN experts and combines them within a shared architecture; it is not a set of arbitrary standalone model endpoints.

### KV cache and latent communication

- **Keep capacity sharing separate from semantic translation.** Existing SwiftCache (`KWRK-000104`) donates idle GPU memory over NVLink for other models’ cache storage; it is not a learned cache-space translator. Existing C2C (`KWRK-000036`) trains projection/fusion components while freezing base LLMs and reports a single-A100, batch-one evaluation; that is not a mixed 8 GB cluster.
- **Same-architecture reuse is narrower.** DroidSpeak (`KWRK-000119`) concerns KV sharing across fine-tuned variants with the same architecture, not arbitrary cross-family translation. KVCOMM (`KWRK-000115`) repairs offsets for cross-context cache reuse; the paper says heterogeneous attention formulations remain underexplored.
- **Cross-model translation has quality and scale conditions.** MoT (`KWRK-000111`) evaluates Llama-3.2, Gemma-3, and Qwen-3 families. Its ten-agent StrategyQA case uses 20 examples; the paper’s compute worker has two H100 80 GB GPUs but each experiment uses one GPU. This is not low-memory edge evidence. The closed-form mapper (`KWRK-000102`) has sharp regressions on two evaluated pairs; CacheBridge (`KWRK-000101`) is a distinct method. Universal Context-Reuse (`KWRK-000114`) reports handoff latency excluding source prefill, which must not be read as end-to-end cost.
- **Benchmarks and counterevidence matter.** KVShareArena (`KWRK-000113`) compares 11 methods and reports that repair quality varies by model and pair; its trained adapter loses quality in 12 of 18 pair–dataset tests. The C2C causal audit (`KWRK-000103`) reports no example-specific transfer for one released projector in its tests. That result is not a universal rebuttal. LatentAlign (`KWRK-000109`) uses frozen 100–400M Gemma-2 models with learned adapters; it does not establish modern low-VRAM performance. LatentMAS (`KWRK-000110`) exchanges latent thoughts/working memory rather than translating arbitrary KV caches. Interlat (`KWRK-000117`) passes hidden-state messages through learned receiver adapters; its “up to 24×” figure concerns communication latency, not whole-system inference speed.
- **TPI-LLM is CPU-device collaboration.** The source describes both emulated and physical testbeds. Its physical case study uses four heterogeneous CPU laptops and full-precision inference. Do not attribute the abstract’s 70B-scale claim or the supplied 26-seconds-per-token note to that physical four-laptop case study; the precise 8-node emulation detail remains unresolved. [arXiv HTML](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.00531), `KWRK-000116`.

### Mistral model identities and training claims

The official pages distinguish **Mistral Large 4**, **Mistral Small 4**, and **Ministral 3**. The reviewed official sources do not identify a “Ministral 4.” Large 4’s company blog rounds the model to 1T total/52B active parameters; the official docs give 1.05T/52B. The blog says it was trained from scratch on 3,800 Grace Blackwell GPUs and announces preview access, but no dollar or GPU-hour training cost is published in the reviewed material. [announcement](https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-large-4/), [model docs](https://docs.mistral.ai/models/mistral-large-4-0), `KWRK-000125`–`KWRK-000126`.

Small 4’s announcement reports 119B total, 128 experts/4 active, and 6B active parameters (8B including embeddings/output); the pinned NVFP4 model card reports 6.5B active. These source-specific values are retained. The card describes post-training activation quantization, not training savings or an 8 GB deployment result. [announcement](https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-small-4/), [pinned model card](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603-NVFP4/tree/45331841b631f4e281df8e959ea3cc9beb84298a), `KWRK-000127`–`KWRK-000128`.

The Ministral 3 technical report (`KWRK-000105`) compares its 1–3T training-token recipe with cited 15T Llama 3 and 36T Qwen 3 figures and reports a 14B base comparison. This is a source-reported token-count comparison, not dollar/GPU-hour savings. The official release and pinned model card identify Ministral 3 as 3B/8B/14B dense models. [technical report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.08584v1), [announcement](https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-3/), [pinned model card](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Ministral-3-14B-Instruct-2512/tree/29439f81c2be264d8d393273f99e7db9c0961120), `KWRK-000129`–`KWRK-000130`.

## Bounded conclusion and open checks

Within the supplied public source set reviewed for this checkpoint, no single verified system combined independent full-model composition, cross-model state transfer, and genuinely low-memory mixed-device execution. This is a scoped search result, not a novelty claim or proof of nonexistence. The historical reconciliation remains partial rather than world-literature coverage.

Outstanding source checks are listed in the [audit](research-intake-audit-2026-10-08.json): SwapMoE’s exact hardware/output behavior; ZipMoE’s exact capacity and imposed-budget matrix; FloE’s exact memory cap; several detailed hardware tables; and TPI-LLM’s 8-node emulation and 70B latency attribution. No private issue crosswalk, inaccessible Notion source, or PR review-thread audit is included.
